_comment: MinusOpsAppPermissionsBoundary -- the ceiling on every role the apply role creates.
A permissions boundary does not GRANT. Effective permissions are the intersection of the
identity policy, this boundary, and any SCP, so a workload role whose identity policy
says iam:* still cannot use it: the boundary does not allow it, and the intersection is
empty. That is what closes `CreateRole` + `AttachRolePolicy` as an escalation path -- the
created role cannot exceed this file no matter what policy Terraform attaches to it.
Scoped to what a DATA PIPELINE WORKLOAD does at runtime: read and write its own data,
run its jobs, log, and alert. Deliberately NOT what Terraform does at deploy time -- a
Glue job has no business creating IAM roles or KMS keys.
Attach it with `iam:PermissionsBoundary` conditions on the apply role, and protect it
from edits with the SCP. This file is the one thing in the whole design that must not be
writable by anything it bounds.
Replace <ACCOUNT_ID>.
What a Glue job, a Step Function, an MWAA environment or a Lambda actually needs to
move data. Read/write on objects, catalog metadata, queues and streams.
USE a key, never manage one. Decrypt and GenerateDataKey let a job read and write
encrypted objects; CreateKey, PutKeyPolicy and ScheduleKeyDeletion are absent, so a
workload role cannot mint a key it controls or destroy one it does not.

Statement._comment: A Glue connection or an MWAA environment attaches ENIs to run in a VPC.

_comment: The escalation cap, stated as a Deny so no attached policy can override it. A role
created inside this boundary cannot create another role, attach a policy, or lift
its own boundary -- which is what stops the chain continuing one level down.
The same set the SCP denies org-wide, repeated here so the boundary alone is
sufficient in an account that has no Organization.
